ANTI-CHEAT UPDATE

v2.9.17Seaside is back

Seaside is open again in single-player and multiplayer, and every map now has laws against playing from places you shouldn't be.

🎃💀📦👥
💣Bomber CubeFrom wave 10: sprints at you and explodes. Shoot it early and it takes its friends with it.
➕Medic CubeFrom wave 20: hangs back and heals the cubes round it. Kill it first.
🛡️Shield CubeFrom wave 25: bullets bounce off its shield. Go round it or use explosives.
🟩Swarm CubesFrom wave 10, now and then: packs of eight tiny, very fast cubes.
🏢Buildings you can go intoOffices, flats and hotels on Frontier and Seaside, with stairs up to the roof. Too many cubes round one and it falls down.
🚀Rocket jumpingShoot the ground at your feet with the Rocket or Pumpkin Launcher to fly up and away.
🛍️New map: MallThree floors of shops round a glass-roofed atrium, escalators, a carpark and shoppers who run from the cubes. Very hard.
🌲New map: ForestDense, dark woods under the moon, with a camp, a cabin and a ruined chapel. Hard.
🏖️New map: SeasideA beach, a pier, the ocean, beach houses and a town. Cubes never come out of the sea.
🎃Pumpkin LauncherLevel 50 of the Battle Pass: a launcher that fires flaming jack-o'-lanterns, with a much bigger blast than the rocket launcher. Limited Edition.
🦇Halloween on every mapJack-o'-lanterns, lights, ghosts, bats and orange trees on every map but Classic, while the event is on.
🔪Knife showcasePick a knife you own to show near the top of your profile. Anyone who opens your profile sees it.
🔒Limited EditionWhen the Halloween 2026 Event ends, the pass locks and Jack's Grin and Reaper's Lantern can't be unlocked any more.
🎃Battle Pass: Halloween 2026 EventThe button in the bottom right of the home screen. 50 levels of coins and knife crates. It ends at the same time for everyone, a week from now.
💀Halloween knivesJack's Grin at level 10 and Reaper's Lantern at level 25. Only in this event, never in crates.
👥Up to 10 playersTeam Deathmatch and C:S Mode rooms grow to fit everyone, up to 5v5.
👥FriendsClick a name in a multiplayer lobby to see their profile and send a friend request. Invite your friends to your games from the Friends button.
💣BombsA new Shop section: the Grenade (pull the pin, click to throw, it blows up on impact) and the Landmine. Pick one as your bomb in the multiplayer loadout.
🔭Extreme Gun scopeRight-click or Z to look down a new scope.
📻Radio · 75 coinsSet it down and it plays 10 upbeat tracks. In multiplayer everyone hears the same song at the same time.
💥Flashbang for goodBuy it once and it's part of your loadout, ready again 20 seconds after each throw.
🪵Barricades onlineBought once now, and they work in multiplayer: everyone sees the planks and can shoot through them.
🎒LoadoutsIn multiplayer, pick 2 pistols and 3 main guns. They go in your hotbar in the order you pick them, on keys 1 to 5.
👑New mode: 1v5Six players: one boss with 2000 health and a shotgun, five attackers with 3 lives each.
🤝Real Co-opEveryone fights the same cubes and the same waves. If anyone goes down, it's game over.
👁️SpectatingOut of the round? Watch any other player through their eyes.
💥Grenades and kitsFlashbangs, smoke grenades, medkits and a defuse kit in the Shop's Utilities.
⚖️Balance changesThe sniper one-shots only with a headshot now, and is wild until you scope in.
🔪125 knife skins75 new ones in every tier, from Tuxedo and Denim up to Ruby, Black Pearl, Golden Cube, Void, Diamond and Plasma Core.
🎯Practice in the lobbyFight cubes on the map while you wait for the round to start.
📦Cheaper crates60 coins each, or open 10 at once for 500.
✊New knife gripA simple fist round the grip, knuckles forward, no twisted wrist.
🌐See their gearIn multiplayer, other players hold the gun they're really using, with their own knife skin.
📦Knife cratesAt the top of the Shop. The reel spins through knife skins and slows down on yours.
✨50 knife skinsCommon 50%, Uncommon 30%, Rare 15%, Super Rare 4.9% and Legendary 0.1%. The cooler the skin, the rarer it is.
🔪New knifeA Counter-Strike style combat knife, held sideways with the blade pointing left, with a new sideways slash.
🛒New ShopTwo sections, Guns and Utilities. Pick anything to see it big, with its stats, and buy it there. You start with just the pistol now: every other gun is in the Shop.
🤠Revolver · 75 coinsThe six-shooter from Russian Roulette. Six rounds that hit hard, and the cylinder turns with every shot.
🪖AK-47 · 110 coinsWooden stock and handguards, the curved magazine, full-auto.
🌀Minigun · 500 coinsSix spinning barrels and 400 rounds. Hold to spin up, and watch the heat: fire too long and it overheats.
🎯Your guns onlineIn multiplayer you pick from the guns you own.
📼Death replaysGet taken out online and you see the last 2 seconds through your killer's eyes while you wait to respawn.
🏅20 new achievementsFor the new guns, big streaks, online kills, replays and more.
🎬Campaign introPress Campaign to watch the opening of the new campaign: the helicopter briefing, the missile, the crash and the fall over the island.
🏜️New map: Dust IIThe classic desert map in multiplayer, for Team Deathmatch, Free-for-all and C:S Mode: long, mid, short, catwalk, the B tunnels and both bomb sites.
🚁Cinematic menuA formation of helicopters flies over the village behind the main menu: the chase ship, the door gunner, the pilot, the man on the skid and the squad in the back.
🎮New menusA big Play button with Shop and Settings under it, each with a picture from the game fading in behind it.
🗺️Play screenCampaign (coming in 3.0), Singleplayer, Multiplayer and Missions, each with its own picture.
🎖️MissionsYour three story missions on their own screen, with a preview of each one.
🥁New soundtrackThe 16-bit tune is gone: a deep, serious war theme with war drums, low strings, brass and a horn melody.
📱iPad modeA new graphics setting made to run smoothly on iPads, and the game runs better on older hardware.
🛒Shop on one screenEverything in a grid of cards, no scrolling.
🎯Scope keyPress Z (or any key you pick) to put the scope up and down instead of holding right click.

v2.9.17a

  • Bug fixes and improvements

v2.9.17 Anti-cheat update

  • Seaside is back, in single-player and multiplayer.
  • New law: no shooting from out of bounds. If you get illegally past a barrier of the map (inside a wall, over the edge, out in the sea, or anywhere the map doesn't let you walk to), your shots can't get through to the other side. An OUT OF BOUNDS warning shows while it's happening.
  • New law: the cubes come for you. If you get somewhere the cubes can't walk to, they stop going round things and come straight through the barriers (and up to your level) for you.
  • Stay out of bounds for 5 seconds and the map puts you back where you last stood.
  • Fixed on Seaside: standing out on the pier made you untouchable, because the cubes couldn't walk onto it. They can now.
  • Fixed on Seaside: a rocket jump could carry you over the line in the shallows (or the pier rails) and out into the sea.
  • Older copies of the game can't join multiplayer games until they refresh.

v2.9.15 Critical update

  • Seaside is down and under construction. The map can't be played for now, in single-player or multiplayer. It will be back in a future update.
  • Older copies of the game can't join multiplayer games until they refresh.

v2.9.14 New cubes

  • Bomber Cube (from wave 10): a black cube with a lit fuse. It sprints at you and blows up when it gets close, and it blows up barricades too. Shoot it early: when it dies it explodes anyway and hurts every cube round it.
  • Medic Cube (from wave 20): a pink cube with white crosses. It keeps its distance and heals the hurt cubes near it with a pink beam. Take it out first.
  • Shield Cube (from wave 25): a teal cube behind a steel shield. Bullets from the front bounce off the shield; hit it from the side or behind, or use the Rocket Launcher, grenades or other explosives.
  • Swarm Cubes (from wave 10, not every wave): packs of eight tiny lime cubes. They're very fast but go down in one hit. Shotgun and Minigun heaven.
  • Buildings you can go into on Frontier (three in the town) and Seaside (three in the town): an office block, flats and a hotel, with furniture on every floor and stairs all the way up to the roof, where a parapet and sandbags make a great spot for snipers. The cubes can follow you in and up. Every front door can be barricaded.
  • Buildings come down: if more than ten cubes crowd round the bottom of a building for a couple of seconds, it shakes and collapses. Anyone inside or on the roof takes a huge hit, and the cubes under it are crushed. It's back for the next game.
  • Forest: the map is now much bigger (250 m across instead of 140 m), with about 1,900 trees, a second cabin with a wrecked pickup, a ranger's lookout, a ring of standing stones and an old army truck.
  • Mall: the escalators up to the 2nd floor now sit beside the ones from the ground floor instead of on top of them, so they no longer look like blocks crossing through each other. More shoppers (including children), staff behind the counters, people eating at the cafe and food court tables, security guards, and shoppers riding the escalators between floors. Brighter shops with posters in the windows, lit window displays, hanging signs and LED strips; benches, bins, plants, vending machines, cash machines and directories in the galleries; a kids' ride; big screens in the atrium playing adverts; and soft shopping-centre music with the sound of the crowd (turn Music off in Settings to mute it).
  • Fixed: some of the Mall's shop signs could come out blank.

    • Balance changes

  • Rocket Launcher and Pumpkin Launcher: rocket jumping. Shoot the ground right at your feet and the blast throws you high into the air and carries you a little way (the Pumpkin Launcher throws you higher). Your own rockets still don't hurt you. Good for getting away, or getting onto a roof.

v2.9.13 Halloween maps

  • New map: Mall. A huge indoor shopping mall on three floors round a tall atrium with a glass roof, and an outdoor carpark. Escalators go up from the atrium to the 1st floor, and from the 1st floor to the 2nd; bridges cross the atrium. 45 shops, each with its own sign and fittings: clothes rails and fitting rooms, shoe walls, a supermarket with aisles, checkouts and fridges, a furniture store, a food court, a cinema, two arcades, a gym, cafes and more.
  • Shoppers: people walk round the Mall, look in the windows and run when a cube gets close. Some cubes go after them. One hit kills them, and that includes yours, so watch where you shoot.
  • New map: Forest. Hundreds of trees close together in the dark, under the moon: a camp in the middle, an old cabin, a ruined chapel with a graveyard, a black pond, fireflies and glowing mushrooms. The cubes are tougher and quicker here.
  • New map: Seaside. A beach with umbrellas, huts and a lifeguard tower, a long pier out over the ocean, a neighbourhood of beach houses (every front door can be barricaded) and a town of tall buildings. Cubes spawn anywhere on land, never in the water.
  • Smarter cubes: on the new maps the cubes find their way round walls, through doorways and up the escalators instead of getting stuck.
  • Barricades in the Mall fit every shop doorway, however wide (the planks stretch to fit), on every floor.
  • Difficulty: every map shows how hard it is: Classic is easy, Frontier, Outpost and Seaside are medium, Forest is hard and the Mall is very hard.
  • Best wave on each map: the map screen shows your best wave on every map. It's no longer on your profile.
  • Legacy: Classic Village has moved to a Legacy section at the bottom of the map screen. It's still there, but the newer maps are better.
  • Halloween decorations on every map but Classic, single-player and multiplayer, while the Halloween 2026 Event is on: jack-o'-lanterns by the front doors, strings of lights round the houses, cobwebs, little graveyards, scarecrows, ghosts and bats, orange trees and a spooky sunset sky.
  • Battle Pass: Jack's Grin is now at level 10 and Reaper's Lantern at level 25. If you were already past those levels, you get them now.
  • Pumpkin Launcher at level 50: a dark grey launcher with two grips and a carved, glowing jack-o'-lantern on the front. It works like the rocket launcher, but it fires flaming pumpkins that leave purple smoke and burst into a much bigger blast with bats and a ghost. Press = to use it. Only in this event: get it before the event ends and it's yours for good; after that it's Limited Edition. It isn't in multiplayer.

v2.9.12 Limited Edition

  • Knife showcase: your profile has a new spot under your level bar. Click it to pick any knife you own, and it shows on your profile. Other players see it when they click your name in a lobby or open your profile from their friends list.
  • The Halloween 2026 Event ends for good: when its timer runs out, the Battle Pass locks and stops giving XP. No new season starts after it.
  • Limited Edition knives: Jack's Grin and Reaper's Lantern become Limited Edition once the event is over. If you got them, they're yours to keep; nobody can unlock them after that.
  • My knives has a new Limited Edition section, right under Stock.

v2.9.11 Halloween 2026 Event

The first Battle Pass, and bigger rooms.

  • Battle Pass: press the new 🎃 Battle Pass button in the bottom right of the home screen. The pass has 50 levels in a straight line. Level up by playing: 3 XP for every coin you earn, 15 XP for every 10 seconds in a game, and 400 XP for every new achievement (250 XP a level).
  • Levels give coins and knife crates (open them from the pass), and some levels give nothing. Level 25 gives Jack's Grin, a carved pumpkin knife with glowing faces, and level 50 gives Reaper's Lantern, a black blade in green ghost-fire with burning skulls, bats and a blood-red edge.
  • Season knives are only in their season and never in knife crates. Once you have one, it's yours to keep.
  • The event lasts one week and the timer is the same for everyone. When it runs out, a new season starts back at level 1 with two new knives.
  • Up to 10 players: Team Deathmatch and C:S Mode rooms now grow to fit everyone who joins, up to 5v5 (1v5 is still exactly 6 players). Free-for-all and Co-op take up to 10.

v2.9.10 Friends & bombs

More groundwork for Cube Assault 3.0: friends, bombs and fixes.

⚖️ Balance changes

  • Extreme Gun: now has a scope (right-click or Z). Scoped in, it zooms like the Sniper Rifle and its shots go dead straight.
  • Friends list: a new Friends button on the main menu. In a multiplayer lobby, click anyone's name to see their profile picture, level, achievements and stats, and send them a friend request. They get a pop-up in the top right to Accept or Decline, and you only become friends if they accept. When you're in a lobby, invite any friend who's online; they get a pop-up to join you.
  • New in the Shop: Bombs, between Guns and Utilities. The Grenade (120 coins): press B to pull the pin, click to throw, and it blows up the moment it hits the ground, a wall, a cube or a player. The Landmine (150 coins): press N to set it down; it blows up when a cube or an enemy player steps on it. Both are bought once and recharge.
  • Multiplayer loadout: a new Bomb section. Pick one bomb to take into the match.
  • Knife crates are cheaper: 50 coins, or 10 for 400.
  • Multiplayer: picking Classic Village now warns that it isn't recommended for online matches.
  • Fixed: public lobbies sometimes said there were none when there were. The list now waits for the lobbies to arrive, and hosts keep their lobby listed after a connection drop.
  • An out-of-date copy now shows error E1 when an online match ends. A match that's already going finishes first.
  • Frontier: cubes no longer spawn behind the mountains.
  • Fixed: the house door frames flickered against the walls, and the Outpost pump house floor flickered through the sand.
  • The Apex Support mission picture now shows the scam cubes, without the floating clouds.
  • The flashbang is multiplayer only now; it no longer shows up in single-player.
  • Settings: the Starting weapon section is gone.

v2.9.9 Radio

More groundwork for Cube Assault 3.0.

⚖️ Balance changes

  • Extreme Gun: now 2500 coins (was 1000). If you already own it, it stays yours.
  • Flashbang: a one-time purchase for 150 coins (was 35 per grenade). It's part of your loadout for good and recharges 20 seconds after each throw. If you had any flashbangs, you own it already.
  • Barricade: a one-time purchase for 150 coins (was 45 each). Use one every 20 seconds. If you had any barricades, you own it already.
  • New in the Shop: the Radio (75 coins). Press R with a full gun (or the knife out) to set it down in single-player or multiplayer, R next to it to pick it up, and E next to it for the next song. 10 upbeat tracks play one after another. In multiplayer everyone hears the same song at the same moment, louder the closer they are. On iPad, tap the radio button.
  • Settings: Radio music On / Off, to mute every radio.
  • Barricades work in multiplayer: board up a house doorway and everyone in the room sees it, bumps into it and can shoot it down.
  • Co-op has no time limit any more: it goes on, wave after wave, until someone dies.
  • Co-op pause: when the host pauses, the cubes stop for everyone, and nobody can hurt them (or be hurt by them) until the host comes back.
  • The first time you load a new version, it opens on that version's patch notes.
  • The FPS counter is on by default (turn it off in Settings).
  • Multiplayer only lets in players on v2.9.9; older copies lock themselves with error E1.

v2.9.8 Ready for 3.0

This version prepares the game's infrastructure and fixes bugs ahead of Cube Assault 3.0.

⚖️ Balance changes

  • Sniper: only a headshot kills in one shot now. A body shot does half health (50 online).
  • Sniper: shots are wildly inaccurate until you scope in (right-click or Z). The Sniper Rifle is unchanged.
  • Loadouts in every multiplayer mode: pick up to 2 pistols (Pistol, Revolver) and up to 3 main guns from the guns you own. The order you pick them is your hotbar: slot 1 is the first one you picked, and so on. In multiplayer the number keys always mean your slots, whatever your keybinds say. The knife is always the last slot. On iPad the touch buttons show your loadout.
  • 20 seconds to get ready when a match starts: pick your loadout and get into position. Nobody can be hurt (or plant the bomb) until it's over.
  • New mode: 1v5. Needs exactly 6 players. One is picked as the boss: 2000 health, a shotgun and nothing else, and a red marker over their head that everyone can see. The other five have 3 lives each; when they're gone, you're out. Guns do the same damage as always (a sniper headshot does 100). The attackers win by killing the boss; the boss wins by taking all their lives or lasting until time runs out.
  • Spectating: when you're out of a round (C:S Mode, 1v5) you watch another player in first person, with their gun. Click (or tap, or press ← →) to switch.
  • Co-op is shared now: the host runs the cubes and the waves and everyone fights the same ones. The cube that's nearest a player goes for them. Kill a cube and the coins are yours. If anyone goes down, it's game over for everyone.
  • Up to 10 players: Team Deathmatch and C:S Mode can be 4v4 or 5v5, and Free-for-all and Co-op take up to 10.
  • Modifiers for the host: Pistols only, Knives only or Snipers only.
  • You can see the gun (or knife skin) every other player is holding.
  • Fixed: the death replay could be cut off by your respawn. Respawns now wait 5 seconds and the replay starts straight away.
  • New in the Shop's Utilities: Flashbang (35 coins, G), Smoke Grenade (35 coins, X), Medkit (60 coins, H) and the Defuse Kit (300 coins, once: C:S Mode only, defuse in 6 seconds instead of 12 as a Counter-Terrorist).
  • Outpost is 50% bigger, with the same look and layout spread out, and more cover.
  • Single-player: the WIP tag is gone from Frontier and the NEW tag from Outpost.
  • An out-of-date copy now locks itself to a black screen (error E1) when you open Multiplayer, until you refresh.

v2.9.7 100 knives

  • 50 new knife skins, 100 in all, spread over every tier: 16 Common, 14 Uncommon, 10 Rare, 6 Super Rare and 4 Legendary (Ruby, Black Pearl, Golden Cube and Void). Every one is different.
  • Knife crates now cost 60 coins. New: Open 10 for 500 coins (instead of 600 one by one); the ten knives flip over one after another, and you can click any of them to equip it.
  • The knife is held in a simple fist with the back of the hand to you and the knuckles forward, and the wrist goes straight into the sleeve.
  • Multiplayer: other players now hold the actual gun they're using, and their knife shows their own skin. The death replay shows the killer's knife skin too.
  • 25 more knife skins, 125 in all, every one different: from Mint Chip and Pinstripe to Synthwave, Code Rain, Comic Pop, Nebula, Chrome, Diamond and Plasma Core.
  • Opening 10 crates now spins the reel for each crate in turn, with the ten filling up underneath (Skip jumps to the end), then shows all ten.
  • Practice while you wait: in a multiplayer lobby, go onto the map and fight cubes until the round starts (no coins for practice). The host can start the round from the Esc menu with Start round.
  • Coins: from wave 5 on, cubes are worth less and less in single-player (half at wave 10, a quarter at wave 20).

v2.9.6 Knife crates

  • New at the top of the Shop: Knife Crates, 75 coins each. The reel spins through the skins and slows down on the one you get.
  • 50 knife skins in five tiers: Common (50%), Uncommon (30%), Rare (15%), Super Rare (4.9%) and Legendary (0.1%). Plain colours are common; camo, patterns and decals are rarer; Fade, Case Hardened, Marble Fade, Lore, Neon Rider and Dragon Scale are Super Rare; Sapphire and Emerald are Legendary.
  • My knives shows your collection. Pick any skin you own to equip it (you need the Knife from the Shop to use it in a game).
  • The knife is remodelled after the Counter-Strike knives: a clip-point blade with a sawback spine, a finger guard, a grooved grip and a lanyard pommel. Your hand now holds it sideways with the blade pointing left, and it slashes across the screen.
  • 4 new achievements for the crates.
  • Fixed: the minigun stayed hot from your last game.
  • Fixed: the minigun's heat bar showed on top of the pause menu.
  • Fixed: in multiplayer you could start a match holding a gun you can't use there; you get the pistol instead.

v2.9.5 The arms dealer

  • The Shop is new: two big buttons, Guns and Utilities. Pick an item to see it up close with its stats, price and key, and buy it or set it as your starting gun right there.
  • You start with only the pistol. The Shotgun (80 coins), Sniper Rifle (120 coins) and Sniper (150 coins) are in the Shop now instead of unlocking at wave 5.
  • New: the Revolver (75 coins, key 9), the AK-47 (110 coins, key 0) and the Minigun (500 coins, key -). The minigun spins up before it fires and overheats if you hold the trigger too long; let it cool down.
  • Multiplayer: when you pick a gun, you pick from the guns you own. In Team Deathmatch and Co-op you carry every gun you own.
  • Multiplayer: when someone takes you out, you watch a replay of the last 2 seconds from their eyes, with their gun, while you wait to respawn.
  • Winning an online match gives you 45 coins.
  • The Shop can't be opened during a game any more, only from the menus.
  • Multiplayer only works on the latest version: older versions can't join any room. Matches already running on an older version carry on until they end.
  • 20 new achievements, in your profile.

v2.9.4 The campaign begins

  • Press Campaign on the Play screen to watch the opening of the new campaign. Sgt. Hale briefs the squad on the helicopter: the cubes have raided the islands and overrun half the military bases. Then the missile hits, the helicopter goes down and you jump.
  • It ends while you're falling over the island with Campaign coming soon: the full campaign arrives in Cube Assault 3.0. Then you're back on the Play screen.
  • The squad look at whoever is talking, and at you, like real people; their eyes blink and the speaker's mouth moves. The helicopter, wind, alarms, explosions and music all play; the characters have no voices, just subtitles.

v2.9.3 Dust II

  • New multiplayer map: Dust II, for Team Deathmatch, Free-for-all and C:S Mode. Terrorists start at T spawn in the south, Counter-Terrorists at CT spawn in the north.
  • Everything is where it should be: long doors, long A and pit, the A car and the blue dumpster, A site with goose and A default, short and its stairs, catwalk above mid, mid doors, xbox, lower and upper B tunnels, B site with B doors, B car and back of B, outside tunnels, T ramp and outside long with its domed building.
  • C:S Mode: the bombs plant on A site and B site, just like the real thing.

v2.9.2 Cinematic menu

  • Multiplayer now checks that you're on the latest version of the game. If a newer version is out, it asks you to refresh the page to update before you can create or join a match, so everyone online plays the same game.
  • The main menu's background is now a cinematic: a formation of helicopters flying over the village, with shots from a chase ship, the door gunner, the pilot, the man on the skid and the squad in the back. On Ultra graphics the far background softens into a haze.

v2.9.1 New soundtrack, iPad mode

  • A new soundtrack: the old 16-bit menu tune is gone. In its place is a deep, serious war theme with heavy war drums, a driving low string pulse, brass chords and a horn melody, all in a big reverb.
  • New in Settings → Graphics: iPad mode. Sharper than Low and keeps the grass, but made to run smoothly on iPads. iPads now start on it.
  • Runs better on older computers and tablets: when the frame rate drops, the game lowers its resolution a little (never below 65%) and updates shadows every other frame, then goes straight back up when it's smooth again. Potato and Ultra are left as they are.
  • The Shop has been rearranged: everything is on one screen in a grid of cards, so you don't have to scroll.
  • New keybind: Scope on / off (Z by default, change it in Settings → Keybinds). It puts the rifle or sniper scope up and takes it down, so you don't have to use right click.

v2.9 New menus

  • A new main screen: a big Play button with Shop and Settings under it, each with a picture from the game fading in behind it.
  • Play opens four choices: Campaign (coming in 3.0), Singleplayer (pick a map and difficulty), Multiplayer and Missions.
  • Missions have their own screen, with a preview of each mission on its button.

v2.8.4 Bug fixes

  • Bug fixes and stability improvements.
  • The Campaign is now called Missions. A brand-new campaign and a new UI are coming in 3.0.

v2.8.3 Chat

  • Multiplayer chat: in a lobby or a match, press Enter, type, and press Enter again to send it to everyone in the room. Esc cancels. Messages fade after a few seconds.

v2.8.2 FPS counter

  • An FPS counter in the top left: green when it's smooth, yellow under 50, red under 30. Turn it off in Settings → FPS counter.
  • Level 3's first aid kit now heals you twice (+40 HP each) before it has to restock.

v2.8.1 First aid

  • Campaign Level 3: there's a first aid kit on a crate back in our trench, by the ladders, with a green cross above it so you can see it from no man's land. Walk up to it for +40 HP; then it takes 25 seconds to restock.

v2.8 Also in this update

  • Apex Support: the sign fits on its board and its phone draws on every computer, and the signs no longer flicker against the walls.
  • The scammers' headsets sit round their heads instead of through them, and the mic bends round the face.
  • The lift no longer rises up through the lobby ceiling and the call-floor slab.
  • Your SWAT team walks through the doors one at a time, and round the desks and walls, instead of through them. They step over the window sill on the way out, too.
  • A much more detailed tower. The lobby has a reception desk with a screen, lamp and bell, a waiting area, columns, a directory board, pictures, a clock and exit signs. The lift has buttons, floor displays and a mirror. The call floor has cubicle panels, phones, mugs, paperwork, PCs, bins, a vending machine, a copier, filing cabinets, a whiteboard, hanging banners, air-con vents and smoke alarms. Outside there's a canopy, air-con units, water tanks and a satellite dish.
  • Three different scam screens on the call-floor computers.
  • Achievements: kill milestones, waves, the big cubes, the campaign levels, the Shop, turrets, barrels, barricades and online matches. Each one is Common (10G), Rare (25G), Epic (50G) or Legendary (100G), and your Profile shows how many you have, your total and your progress on the rest.
  • Achievements you'd already earned before this update (kills, best wave, campaign levels) unlock straight away.
  • Your best kill badge sits next to your name on your Profile.
  • Public lobbies: when you create a match, choose Public (recommended) or Private. Public lobbies are listed live under Multiplayer → Public lobbies with the host, mode, map and players; lobbies that are full, locked, mid-match or on another version show but can't be joined, and ones with a password ask for it.
  • Mission loading screens: the level, title, place and briefing animate in with a loading bar, then the black splits open into the cutscene.
  • Health packs dropped on a step or high ground stay there, and you can pick them up.
  • Fix: a barrel on a map you weren't playing could go off if a rocket landed in the same spot on yours.
  • Fix: no more "Wave cleared" banner in campaign missions that don't have waves.
Older updates

v2.7.2 Barrels & barricades

  • Exploding barrels: shoot a red barrel once and it leaks fuel; shoot it again and it blows up, hurting cubes and you nearby. Rockets set them off too.
  • Barricades (100 coins): buy them in the Shop, stand in a house doorway and press J, and your hands screw planks over the door to keep the cubes out.
  • A barricade has 100 HP. Cubes batter it down, the Angry Cube goes straight through, and your own bullets break it too.
  • Scope lock, new in Settings: click once to scope in and it stays until you click again. Easier on trackpads and iPads.

v2.7.1 The Angry Cube

  • New cube: the Angry Cube, a grey cube that smashes straight through house walls, trees and buildings. One arrives at wave 20, then one every 5 waves.
  • Cubes jump over fences (like the ones round the wheat farm) and crates to reach you, and jump up after you onto crates.
  • A slightly higher jump makes crates easy to stand on, and you can climb a stack of two from a single crate.
  • The purple Brute Cube has twice the health.

v2.7 New hands

  • New first-person hands: tactical gloves with knuckle pads and wrist straps, and sleeves down to the gloves, holding every gun the way soldiers do in modern shooters.
  • The rifle has a scope, like the sniper's. Right-click (or tap the aim button on touch) to aim through it; it zooms in less than the sniper.
  • A new-look pistol: a dark slide on a tan frame, with serrations, a rail and a flared grip, held lower and straighter.
  • The knife is held on the right with the blade up and pokes straight forward.
  • New patch notes and What's new screens.

v2.6.3 Fixes

  • Online gunshots and their sounds no longer lag: the first shot of every burst is sent straight away instead of waiting for the next network update, so other players see and hear your shots, and you get your hit markers, about 3 to 4 times sooner.
  • Fixed a match sometimes ending straight away as a draw if the host pressed Start just as someone was still connecting.
  • Other players' models are lighter to draw, for smoother frame rates on school laptops.

v2.6.2 C:S Mode

  • The rifle is now a choice for your main gun in C:S Mode, alongside the shotgun, sniper and rocket launcher. Each choice shows a 3D picture of the gun.
  • Other players are now low-poly people instead of cubes. There are 6 looks and everyone in a room gets their own, with a band in their team colour.
  • Enemies have a red dot above their name tag.
  • When a match is won, a victory scene plays on the map for everyone: the winning team (or the Free-for-all winner) celebrates up front with the losers standing behind them, under a big VICTORY or DEFEAT. Then the scores show. Click, tap or press Space to skip it.
  • Winning an online match, as a team or on your own, gives you 50 coins. Losing gives none. (45 coins since 2.9.5.)
  • Single-player and the campaign are unchanged.

v2.6.1 C:S Mode

  • New multiplayer mode: C:S Mode, on the Outpost. Two teams, Terrorists (orange) and Counter-Terrorists (blue), play rounds. The host picks 3, 5 or 8 rounds to win.
  • Terrorists: stand in site A or site B and hold E (or the E button on touch) for 3 seconds to plant the bomb, then guard it. If it explodes after 60 seconds, the Terrorists win the round.
  • Counter-Terrorists: defend both sites. If the bomb is planted, find it and hold E for 12 seconds to defuse it. Stopping the plant until the round timer runs out also wins the round.
  • Either team also wins a round by taking out everyone on the other side (once the bomb is planted, the Counter-Terrorists still have to defuse it). If you're taken out, you're back at the start of the next round.
  • Starting gun choice in C:S Mode and Free-for-all: everyone gets a pistol and a knife, and picks one more gun when the match starts: shotgun, sniper or rocket launcher.
  • No Extreme Gun and no turrets when fighting other players. In Co-op against the cube waves you can use your Extreme Gun and turret again, if you own them.

v2.6 Real online multiplayer

  • Multiplayer is live: create a match, share the 5-letter code, and up to 6 friends can join from their own computers, tablets or phones. No more practice bots.
  • Team Deathmatch and Free-for-all with real hits, deaths, respawns and scores. Everyone gets the same guns: pistol, rifle, shotgun, sniper, knife and rocket launcher.
  • Co-op: play the cube waves side by side on the same map (each player fights their own cubes for now).
  • Rockets blow the same holes in everyone's map, and players who join late see them too.
  • Other players glide smoothly even on a slow connection, your own movement never waits for the internet, and shots count where you saw the other player.
  • If the host leaves, the next player takes over and the match carries on.
  • Works on school networks (no special ports). Press F3 in a match for network stats.

v2.5 Multiplayer and Outpost

  • New Multiplayer button on the main menu. Create a match to get a 5-letter room code (with an optional password), or join a friend's match by typing their code.
  • Multiplayer is a preview for now: matches are filled with practice bots, and real online play with friends is coming in a later update.
  • The lobby has Red and Blue teams (tap a team to switch), and the host picks the mode (Team Deathmatch, Free-for-all or Co-op waves), team size (1v1, 2v2, 3v3), map, kill limit, time limit, friendly fire and whether the room is locked. The host can also auto-balance teams and kick players.
  • In a match: hold Tab (or tap Scores on touch) for the scoreboard, plus a kill feed, team-coloured name tags, a ping indicator and a respawn countdown. A results screen at the end lets you rematch or leave.
  • New map: Outpost, a desert compound with Red and Blue spawns at opposite ends, three lanes, chokepoints, two crate-filled sites (A and B), a pump house in the middle and four watchtowers. Play it in single-player too, from the map screen.
  • The "playing now" counter is back on the main menu.

v2.4 Hard mode

  • Endless now has two difficulties, picked on the map screen. Hard: cubes have 70% more health and 40% more of them spawn each wave.
  • New enemy from wave 20: the Splitter Cube, a giant orange cube that splits into two smaller cubes when destroyed, three times over. Another one joins every fifth wave after that.
  • On a phone or tablet, the game now asks the first time whether you want touch controls.

v2.3 Play anywhere

  • Cube Assault now works on phones and tablets. Touch controls: a joystick on the left to move (push it all the way to sprint), drag anywhere on the right to look, and buttons for fire, jump, reload, the sniper scope, your turret, holding E in the campaign, and pause.
  • Tap a gun in the bar at the bottom of the screen to switch to it. Drag your thumb while holding Fire to aim and shoot at the same time. With the knife, swipe to slash.
  • The game spots phones and tablets by itself. Settings → Touch controls lets you pick Auto, On or Off.
  • Phones start on Low graphics the first time, so the game runs smoothly. You can change it in Settings.
  • Menus fit on short screens, like a phone held sideways, and scroll by touch.
  • Fix: scrolling the mouse wheel when you only had one gun (as in the campaign) cancelled your reload.

v2.2 Bring it down

  • Apex Support has a new ending if you throw the last scammer out of the window: a ladder rolls out of the broken window, your team climbs down to the street, and Captain Mehta has one last idea.
  • A line of dynamite runs from the tower's front door. Shoot the TNT box at the end of the fuse, watch it burn all the way to the tower, and bring the whole call centre down.

v2.1 Backup has arrived

  • Your SWAT team now joins the raid on Apex Support: Mehta, Singh and D'Souza move through the call centre and open fire on the scammers alongside you. (The cubes are still yours to take down.)
  • Fix: black flickering stripes on the call-centre ceiling.
  • Fix: the call-centre walls flickered where the window pillars met the sills, and the lift doors flickered while sliding.

v2.0 Campaign: Level 2

  • New campaign level: Level 2, Apex Support (Mumbai, India, 2009). You're a SWAT officer raiding a scam call centre at the top of a tower.
  • A long opening cutscene: walk up to the tower with your three-officer SWAT team, sneak through the lobby, ride the lift to the fifth floor and spy on the scammers from behind a wall while they work their phones. Then Captain Mehta counts to three.
  • New enemy, campaign only: Scam Cubes. Yellow cubes with happy faces and headsets, about twenty of them at their computers. When the raid starts they jump off their chairs and come for you.
  • Take down every scammer but the last, and you grab him. He begs, offers you a bribe, and you decide what happens next. Choose carefully.
  • Campaign levels now unlock in order: finish Level 1 to open Level 2.
  • Fix: the campaign's Level complete and Mission failed screens always talked about Level 1.

v1.9.2 Menu music

  • The menus now have music: a fast, catchy 16-bit style track made from the game's own sound engine, so it still works offline. It fades in on the menus and fades out when a game starts.
  • New in Settings: Music On / Off.

v1.9.1 Campaign

  • Fix: in the normal maps (Classic Village and Frontier) you died about a second after the first wave started. This bug came in with v1.9 and is now fixed.
  • The Birch Road (Russia, 1944) now has 5 waves instead of 3: 4, 5, 6, 7 and then 9 Rifle Cubes, with +25 HP between waves.

v1.9 Campaign

  • New Campaign mode at the top of the Play screen. Five story levels are planned: Level 1 is playable now, and the rest say Coming soon.
  • Level 1, The Birch Road (Russia, 1944): it opens with a title card, then a cutscene. You ride in the passenger seat of an army jeep while your comrade, Sergeant Volkov, drives and talks, with his lines typed out at the bottom of the screen. Keyboard and mouse are locked until the jeep stops.
  • Cubes are spotted, the jeep stops and you jump out with a rifle. Hold the road against waves of Rifle Cubes, red cubes that carry guns (only in this level, never in the normal maps). Then push into the cube camp and hold E to claim their flag.
  • A new snowy map made just for this level, with falling snow, a birch forest, log cabins, anti-tank barricades and the cube camp.
  • If you fall, Retry level puts you straight back at the jeep without the cutscene. Finished levels are ticked off on the Play screen.

v1.8.1 Shop update

  • The Knife is back in the Shop for 50 coins.
  • The Rocket Launcher is now in the Shop for 250 coins.
  • The Turret is cheaper: 200 coins instead of 400.
  • Fix: the knife could hit cubes through walls.
  • Fix: switching to an empty gun (like the rocket launcher after a shot) now starts reloading straight away instead of waiting for you to click.
  • Fix: cubes thrown into the air by a rocket could still hurt you while flying over your head.

v1.8 Physics

  • New weapon: the Rocket Launcher (press 8). One rocket at a time with a 3-second reload. The blast hurts every cube nearby and throws the survivors into the air.
  • Destructible maps: rockets blow holes in houses, buildings and trees. Whatever is inside the blast breaks into small blocks that tumble and bounce to the ground. The damage stays until you quit the round or die.
  • New weapon: the Knife (press 7). You don't have to hold the key: press 7 once, then swipe the mouse or trackpad (or click) to slash.
  • The Extreme Gun now holds 200 rounds instead of 50.
  • A What's new screen now pops up the first time you open a new version.
  • Weapon keys are now fixed: 1 to 5 for the guns, 6 for the turret, 7 for the knife and 8 for the rocket launcher.
  • Fix: a bright line of light leaked along the top of the walls inside houses.
  • Fix: banners cut each other off, for example Level up hiding the new wave. They now show one after another.

Removed

  • The list of controls on the main menu.

v1.7.1 Turret & fixes

  • New in the Shop: the Turret (400 coins). Press 6 in a game to set it down next to you. It shoots the nearest cube it can see once a second, and any normal cube goes down in two hits. The King only takes a scratch from each shot.
  • Your turret has 200 HP, double yours, and never heals. Cubes will go for it if it's closer than you, and enemy shots and the King's shockwave hurt it. Its health shows above yours, and it appears on the radar. You can only have one out at a time.
  • Fix: from inside a house, the ceiling showed the roof tiles stretched into a spiderweb pattern. Houses now have proper wooden ceilings.
  • Fix: the top of every doorway flickered where the door frame met the wall.
  • Windows now show on the inside walls of houses too, not just outside.
  • Fix: window bars flickered against the glass from a distance, and on Frontier the town's streets flickered against the paving.

v1.7 Frontier

  • Pressing Play now lets you choose a map: Classic Village (the original map) or Frontier.
  • Frontier (work in progress) is four times the size of the classic map. It has the village in the middle, a dense forest, a mountain range, a town of tall buildings and parked cars, and a farm with a barn and fenced fields.
  • You always start in the middle of the village, on both maps.
  • On Frontier, cubes spawn 30 to 50 metres from you instead of at the outer wall, so you're not waiting for them to cross the map.

v1.6.3 Pop!

  • The Shotgun and Sniper now unlock when you reach wave 5 in every game, instead of staying unlocked forever. Every game starts with the Pistol and Rifle, plus the Extreme Gun if you've bought it.
  • New sounds: destroyed cubes now burst with a punchy pop and rattling debris, deeper for bigger cubes. Every gun also has its own sound when you switch to it.
  • Fix: the snow on the mountains flickered and had ragged streaks, because it sat exactly on the rock.
  • Fix: clouds drifted straight through the mountains and jumped from one side of the sky to the other. They now circle slowly over the village.

v1.6.2 Fresh start

  • You now start with the Pistol and Rifle. Reach wave 5 to unlock the Shotgun and Sniper for good. If you've already reached wave 5, they're already unlocked.
  • New in Settings: Reset all data. After a warning screen, it wipes your name, level, stats, coins, guns and settings and starts the game fresh.
  • Fix: if your browser blocked mouse capture, the message telling you what to do never appeared. It now shows at the bottom of the screen.
  • Fix: the kill-combo counter stayed on screen behind the game-over screen.

v1.6.1 Fixes & polish

  • The Extreme Gun now costs 1,000 coins (was 100). If you already own it, you keep it.
  • Fix: a big hit near the edge of the map could knock a cube through the outer wall, where it got stuck and the wave never ended.
  • Fix: destroyed cubes and enemy energy shots weren't cleared from memory, so long sessions slowly got slower.
  • Your best wave now counts when you quit to the menu, not only when you die.
  • The new-wave banner now shows how much health you actually got back, or "Full health".

v1.6 Profiles

  • Profiles: the game asks for your name the first time you play. Click your profile in the top right of the main menu to see it.
  • Your profile tracks every game you play: level, total accuracy, shots fired, cubes killed, time played and best wave.
  • Levels: every point you score is XP. You'll see a banner mid-fight when you level up.
  • Profile pictures: choose from 3D portraits of things in the game, including every cube, the King, all five guns, a crate, a barrel, a tree and a health pack.

v1.5.1 Hands on

  • You can now see your arms and hands. Every gun is held properly: trigger finger on the trigger, the other hand on the handguard, pump or forend, and both hands on the pistol.
  • Animated reloads: your free hand pulls the old magazine, grabs a fresh one and pushes it home. On the shotgun it feeds shells in one at a time, and on the sniper your hand works the bolt after every shot.
  • Your gun and arms now stay a sensible size at any field of view, instead of shrinking at wide settings and filling the screen at narrow ones.
  • Two new graphics options. Ultra: sharper image, crisper shadows, thicker grass and a longer view distance. Potato: low resolution, flat colours and no shadows or grass, for slow computers.

v1.5 Real guns

  • All five weapons rebuilt in detail at real-world size: Glock-style pistol, AR-15 rifle with red-dot sight, pump shotgun with walnut stock, bolt-action sniper with a glass-lensed scope, and a sleeker Extreme Gun.
  • Reflective metal, stippled grips, knurled turrets and wood grain.
  • The pistol slide kicks back, the shotgun pumps and the sniper bolt cycles after every shot.
  • Brass shells eject and clink on the ground; magazines drop out and get swapped when you reload.
  • The game now works fully offline from the downloaded file.

v1.4 The King arrives

  • New boss: the King Cube storms in on wave 15 and every 5 waves after. Jump over its shockwave. It's worth 10 coins.
  • Radar at the top of the screen shows every cube, enemy shot and health pack near you.
  • Kill combos: chain kills within 2.5 seconds to multiply your score, up to ×5.
  • Cubes sometimes drop health packs (+30 HP). Brutes drop them more often.
  • Switch weapons with the scroll wheel, or press Q to swap back to your last one.
  • End-of-game stats: kills, accuracy, best combo, and a "New best" flag.
  • Balance: fewer Blue Cubes per wave early on, and Brutes arrive in smaller groups.
  • Fix: the game now pauses itself when you switch to another tab or window.

v1.3 Looks & sound

  • New sky, clouds, mountains, forest, swaying grass and textured buildings.
  • Sound effects, damage numbers, hit markers, recoil, screen shake and a Graphics: Low option.
  • Fix: your gun no longer pokes through walls.

v1.2 Mouse fix

  • The mouse now locks as soon as you press Play, and the game tells you if your browser blocks it.

v1.1 New cubes & the village

  • Green, Blue and Brute cubes, each with an intro screen.
  • Houses, trees and cover; coins, the Shop and the Extreme Gun.

v1.0 First release

  • Four weapons, red cubes, waves and settings.

Extreme Gun

Full-auto plasma rifle. Every shot explodes on impact and damages every cube nearby.

Turret

Press 6 in a game to set it down next to you. It shoots the nearest cube once a second, and any normal cube goes down in two hits. It has 200 HP, double yours, and never heals. One at a time, or two at once after wave 15.

Barricade

Stand in a house doorway and press J to board it up with planks. Cubes have to break through it (100 HP), and so do your bullets. One use each.

Knife

Press 7 in a game, then flick the mouse or trackpad (or click) to slash. Short reach, never runs out, and one slash takes out a Red Cube.

Rocket Launcher

Press 8 in a game. One rocket at a time with a 3-second reload. The blast hurts every cube nearby and blows holes in houses, buildings and trees.

Use touch controls?

Reset all data?

This permanently deletes everything: your name, level, stats, coins, best wave, unlocked and bought guns, profile picture and settings. The game restarts as if you'd never played.

This can't be undone.

Data
Coming in Cube Assault 3.0

Cube Assault is changing in 3.0

Cube Assault 3.0 is a big one: the game is changing significantly. It brings a brand-new, detailed campaign with a full story, more levels and bigger battles, and a completely new UI across the menus and the game. It will be rolled out soon.

Until then, the current story levels have been renamed Missions. You can still play all of them from the Play screen, and your progress is kept.

Coming in Cube Assault 3.0

The Campaign isn’t out yet

A brand-new, detailed campaign with a full story is being built for Cube Assault 3.0, and it isn’t released yet. Until then, try the Missions.
